# Results — Study 889 (Broad Dollar-Hedge Overlay)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **generalise
[study 613](../../613-currency-hedged-etf-carry/)** (which showed the hedged-minus-unhedged gap for
ONE market, Japan, is the covered-interest-parity rate differential) to **broad developed
international** (MSCI EAFE): is `hedged − unhedged` the (now positive, dollar-favourable)
US-vs-foreign short-rate differential, mechanically — and does a systematic "hedge when the US
out-yields" overlay add Sharpe once costed? Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. Data as-of 2026-06-30 — **as-of 2026-06-30**
(the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `7afa89fb9f2f`
(monthly panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance monthly total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`), **HEFA / EFA / DBEF / IEFA / UUP / BIL** + `^IRX`, plus **EUR/JPY/GBP/CHF spot** for the currency basket, 2011-01 → 2026-06 |
| Clean pair | **HEFA vs EFA** (2014-03+, n=148) — iShares Currency Hedged MSCI EAFE literally *holds EFA + one-month FX forwards*: the **same basket**, so the return gap is the hedge P&L almost purely (the broad analogue of 613's HEWJ/EWJ) |
| Long pair | **DBEF vs EFA** (2011-07+, n=180) — Xtrackers MSCI EAFE Hedged vs iShares MSCI EAFE (same index, different provider) — a longer tape spanning the US-under-yields → US-out-yields flip |
| fx_foreign | **spot** USD return of an EAFE-weighted currency basket (EUR .40 / JPY .25 / GBP .20 / CHF .15). `carry_hat = (hedged − unhedged) + fx_foreign` |
| Rates | US = `^IRX` (13-week bill, %); foreign = an EAFE-weighted **policy-rate blend** (ECB .40 / BOJ .25 / BOE .20 / SNB .15, hardcoded step tables, sources cited) |
| Overlay / costs | one documented lag: hold **hedged** when the *prior* month-end US−foreign differential > 0, else unhedged; a full switch costs 2 × one-way bps; the isolation spread pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the carry mean and on the hedge regression `diff = α + β·(−fx)`; a block-bootstrap Sharpe/mean CI; a 2022 era split; a 20-seed synthetic control |

> **Why spot and not UUP for the carry.** The identity `carry_hat = diff + fx_foreign` needs the
> pure **spot** return of the foreign basket. `UUP`'s *total* return also earns the US-bill
> collateral yield, so a naive `carry_hat = diff − UUP` subtracts that yield and **cancels most of
> the carry** — it prints *negative*, worst in the high-rate 2022+ era (−2.2 %/yr). The spot basket
> avoids the trap; the notebook keeps the UUP version as a worked cautionary tale.

> **Young ETF / one-regime caveat (Signal axis).** HEFA's clean tape starts **2014-03** (148
> months). The whole sample sits in an era where the US *out-yielded* EAFE and the dollar broadly
> *rose*, so the raw hedged-sleeve win is part mechanical carry, part a single realised dollar
> regime. The robust, regime-independent leg is the **carry identity** below.

## The identity — `carry_hat = (hedged − unhedged) + fx_foreign` ≈ the rate differential

| pair | n | carry_hat (%/yr) | HAC *t* | observed rate diff | β on −fx | *t*(β) | R² | boot 95% CI | frac ≤ 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|--:|
| **HEFA/EFA** (same basket) | 148 | **+1.68** | **+4.74** | +1.35 | **0.93** | +34.8 | 0.91 | **[+0.90, +2.45]** | 0.000 |
| DBEF/EFA (provider diff) | 180 | +1.37 | +2.56 | +1.09 | 0.90 | +27.8 | 0.69 | [−0.02, +2.84] | 0.027 |

**The identity generalises.** On the clean same-basket pair the currency hedge is a near-full short
of the foreign basket (β = 0.93, R² = 0.91) and the residual carry is **+1.68 %/yr at HAC
*t* = +4.74**, sitting right on the **observable +1.35 %/yr** policy differential; the bootstrap CI
clears zero. The longer DBEF pair corroborates (β = 0.90, carry +1.37 %/yr, *t* = +2.56) with more
basket noise. This is the broad-EAFE version of 613's Japan result — now with a **positive,
dollar-favourable** differential.

## Era split (cut 2022-01-01 — the dollar/rate regime flip)

| pair | era | n | carry_hat (%/yr) | HAC *t* | obs rate diff |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| HEFA/EFA | pre-2022 | 94 | +1.15 | **+2.89** | +0.89 |
| HEFA/EFA | 2022+ | 54 | +2.61 | **+4.88** | +2.14 |
| DBEF/EFA | pre-2022 | 126 | +1.00 | +1.43 | +0.64 |
| DBEF/EFA | 2022+ | 54 | +2.22 | **+3.88** | +2.14 |

On the clean pair the carry clears *t* ≥ 2 in **both** halves and **grows with the differential**
(+1.15 → +2.61 %/yr as the gap widened +0.89 → +2.14 %/yr) — the mechanical, not-one-era signature.

## The excess-of-cash Sharpe race (both legs minus BIL)

| pair | hedged Sharpe (95% CI) | unhedged Sharpe (95% CI) | advantage | max DD hedged / unhedged |
|---|:--:|:--:|--:|--:|
| HEFA/EFA | 0.75 [0.20, 1.35] | 0.40 [−0.11, 0.95] | **+0.35** | −20.7% / −27.6% |
| DBEF/EFA | 0.75 [0.27, 1.27] | 0.42 [−0.07, 0.93] | +0.32 | −20.7% / −27.6% |

The hedged sleeve out-Sharped the unhedged one and cut the drawdown — but the two CIs **overlap**,
so the Sharpe *advantage* is not on its own robustly distinguishable from a lucky dollar decade. The
regime-independent evidence is the carry, not the realised Sharpe gap.

## The "hedge when the US out-yields" overlay (HEFA/EFA)

Signal = prior-month US−foreign differential > 0; one lag; costed at 3 bps one-way.

| | switches | share hedged | Sharpe ex-cash | adv vs unhedged | adv vs hedged |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| overlay | **1** | 0.93 | 0.67 | +0.27 | **−0.08** |
| always-hedged | — | 1.00 | **0.75** | — | — |
| always-unhedged | — | 0.00 | 0.40 | — | — |

**The switch adds nothing.** The US has out-yielded EAFE for ~93 % of the post-2014 sample, so the
overlay fires **once in twelve years** — it is effectively "always hedge", and its brief unhedged
spell only *lowers* the Sharpe below always-hedging (−0.08). There is no differential-timing edge
here to harvest; the decision that matters is simply *to hedge*, and the differential tells you the
carry is positive, not *when* to flip.

## Isolating the carry — long hedged / short unhedged (= long the dollar), costed

| net (%/yr) | HAC *t* | charge (%/yr) |
|--:|--:|--:|
| **+2.53** | **+1.41** | 0.62 |

To bank *only* the carry you would short the unhedged twin — but that spread is long the dollar (a
currency bet), and the fx volatility it carries swamps the ~1.7 %/yr carry: it nets +2.53 %/yr at
only *t* = +1.41. The clean carry is real but not cleanly *isolable* as a market-neutral spread.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic monthly world with a planted hedge carry (knob `carry_annual`) plus an fx leg. No
network.

| world | recovered carry | HAC *t* | hedge β |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`carry = 0`), **20 seeds** | ~0 | mean **+0.03** (sd 0.89), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20** | — |
| planted (`carry = +3 %/yr`) | **+2.56 %/yr** | **+7.08** | 1.00 |

The estimator recovers a *planted* carry with β ≈ 1 and never fires on the null — so the real-tape
carry is a genuine mechanical pickup, not machinery. *(A faithful-engine check only — never cited in
support of the stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The 613 currency-hedge carry identity **generalises to broad developed
  international**. On the clean same-basket HEFA/EFA pair the hedge is a near-full short of the
  foreign basket (β = 0.93, R² = 0.91) and pockets **+1.68 %/yr at HAC *t* = +4.74** — right on the
  observable +1.35 %/yr policy differential — with a bootstrap CI clear of zero (**[+0.90, +2.45]**)
  and *t* ≥ 2 in **both** eras (+2.89 / +4.88), growing with the differential. The longer DBEF pair
  corroborates (*t* = +2.56). This is a genuine, dollar-favourable mechanical premium. *(One-regime
  caveat: the sample is a single US-out-yields / rising-dollar era; the carry identity is the
  regime-independent part, the raw Sharpe win is not.)*
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The carry is real, positive, and cheap to *hold* (the hedged wrapper's
  expense gap over the unhedged twin is ~2 bp), but it is **not bankable as an overlay**: (1) the
  "hedge when the US out-yields" **switch adds nothing** over just always-hedging — the US
  out-yielded EAFE ~93 % of months (1 switch in 12 yr), so there is no differential-timing edge; (2)
  the excess-Sharpe advantage's CI overlaps and rests on one realised dollar regime; (3) isolating
  the pure carry is a dollar-long spread that nets +2.53 %/yr at only *t* = +1.41 (fx vol swamps it).
  Real but thin and un-timeable → **Fragile**, not Investable.
